# Agent notes

This repository is an OpenCode plugin. Read the README for what it does; this file is for working on it.

## Layout and checks

- `src/` is the plugin, `test/` the suites, `scripts/` the checks. `npm run check` runs typecheck, unit, build, icons,
  host, pack, forbidden, copies, whitelist and actionlint, in that order.
- `npm run check` with `OPENCODE_BIN_2_2_3` to `OPENCODE_BIN_2_2_6` set runs the host and pack stages against every
  tested release; once unset it falls back to the locked SDK with a notice.
- `npm run drift` compares the plugin's tool table with `test/fixtures/live-tools.json`.
- The host suite needs Bun 1.4.4 and Node 24. It starts an embedded OpenCode, so it must not run against a real account:
  the fake server is loopback only, and any fetch that leaves loopback fails the run.

## Forbidden in this repository

Checked by `scripts/check-forbidden.mjs` across `src/`, `test/`, `scripts/` and `dist/`:

- fork-only markers (`dispatch-lease`, `catalog-ownership`, text-only response markers), `options.mcp` delegation,
  `Plugin.image`, imported OAuth grants;
- the V1 plugin API (`@opencode-ai/*`), V1 hooks (`tool.execute.before`, `chat.message`, `permission.ask`),
  `ctx.generate.text`, `experimental.policies`, and `@opencode/ai`;
- a permission hook other than the tools RPC's one evaluate hook;
- private host source paths and host checkouts;
- machine-local home and temp paths;
- internal process wording: who decided what, lane names, ticket references of our own.

## House rules

- `src/host/tools-rpc.ts` is a copy of a module several plugins share. Edit only between its `PLUGIN-SPECIFIC` markers;
  `npm run check` fails the copies stage otherwise. The same goes for `test/support/jelly-kit.ts` and
  `test/support/jelly-settings.ts`.
- The tool table is `src/elevenlabs-tools.ts` and nothing else: the default rules, the tools RPC, status, the spending
  guard, the Jelly declaration and the tests all derive from it.
- Every error the plugin raises has a code from `PLUGIN_CODES`, and the README's and the configuration guide's tables
  must match it exactly.
- The plugin never sees the OAuth token, and never prints one. Anything read from the network goes through
  `src/redact.ts` before it reaches status or the session.
- A tool that writes asserts its own permission inside `execute`; a declared `permission` alone does not ask.
- The tool table and the estimate's shape were measured in live reconcile 1 (`test/fixtures/README.md`): the catalogue
  is the live one, an estimate costs nothing but creates a flow, and its figure is the batch total and may be
  fractional. One fact is still unverified, and the README's Known limits is the one place that says so: whether a paid
  result reports what it really cost, and in which field. Do not state that as settled, and do not call the tool table
  provisional.
- The icon `assets/icon.svg` (and the two PNGs rendered from it) is ElevenLabs' "11" symbol from https://elevenlabs.io/brand,
  used under those guidelines: the symbol unmodified (black, only scaled, its path data pre-scaled to the family's 48 grid)
  on a neutral holding shape whose height is three times the symbol's. Do not recolour, redraw or combine it, and keep the
  README's trademark line.
- Releases come only from `.github/workflows/release.yml` ("Releasing" in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)). A
  release-prep PR sets `version` in `package.json` and the install specs and runs `node scripts/changelog.mjs release`;
  once it is on `master` and CI passed, start the release with
  `gh workflow run release.yml --ref master -f sha=<its full sha>`. The workflow builds `dist/`, makes the release
  commit on a temporary `release/v<version>` branch, checks and stages everything, and waits for the owner to approve
  the `release` environment; only then does it create the tag `v<version>` and the GitHub Release. Never push a tag or a
  `release/*` branch, and never commit, tag or publish a release by hand. Agents never approve a release, never call the
  deployment-approval API, and never bypass a ruleset or the environment.
- No personal email in anything we publish. Every commit is authored and committed as
  `joe-broadhead <91376460+joe-broadhead@users.noreply.github.com>`, except the release commit and tag, which the
  release workflow makes as `github-actions[bot]`. Before committing or tagging, check that
  `git config user.email` is that address: a fresh clone inherits the machine's global identity, which is not that
  address. Never commit, tag or publish with a work or personal address, or with a local hostname.

# ElevenLabs call review

A conversation holds a real person's words, the identifier your integration gave them, the phone number they called from,
whatever the agent was told to extract, and the variables their app passed in. Treat all of it as personal data about
someone who did not choose to talk to a model.

## Reading

- `agents_list_conversations` for the calls themselves: agent, time, duration, outcome. Start here.
- `agents_get_conversation` with a `conversation_id` for one call: the transcript turns, the post-call summary, the
  extracted fields, and `cost` in credits beside `cost_fiat` in dollars.
- `agents_search_conversation_messages` searches the words across calls, and
  `agents_semantic_search_conversation_messages` searches by meaning. Use them when the user remembers what was said,
  not which call it was.
- `agents_get_conversation_summary` gives the post-call summary alone, which is often enough and carries less of the
  caller's own words.

## Reporting

- **Summarise; do not dump.** Quote at most the turns that carry the finding, and say which call and when.
- Never copy a caller's name, number, address or extracted field into another tool, a file, a commit, a message or a public
  page. Keep the call id and let the user open the call.
- Never send transcript text to a web search, a research tool or an external service.
- If the answer needs who the person is, give the call id and the time; the user can open it in the ElevenLabs app.
- An empty result means no call matched within the user's access and the filters used. Say that; do not guess a cause.

## The `conversations` option

The plugin can deny these reads without denying the metadata ones. `conversations: "summary"` denies the four tools
that return a caller's words — `agents_get_conversation`, `agents_get_conversation_summary`,
`agents_search_conversation_messages` and `agents_semantic_search_conversation_messages` — and keeps the counts and the
listings. `"off"` denies those and every other conversation read, `agents_list_conversations`, `agents_list_memories`
and the triage tickets included. If a call is refused, the option or a rule stopped it - say so and name the option, and
do not try another route to the same words.

## Cost

A conversation's `cost` is ElevenLabs credits, and `cost_fiat` is dollars. Report credits as credits; the plugin never
converts one to the other.

## Not this skill

The user's own meetings are Granola, Wispr Flow or Plaud. Changing what an agent says is the `elevenlabs` skill.

# ElevenLabs generation

Generations land on a **Flow**, the editable canvas that holds the prompt and the results. They **spend the workspace's
credits**, so read this first. Every tool takes a `context` parameter: one short line naming the goal.

## What spends

Twelve tools bill the workspace: `creative_generate_speech`, `creative_generate_image`, `creative_generate_video`,
`creative_edit_image`, `creative_generate_in_flow`, `creative_run_flow_nodes`, `creative_transcribe_audio`,
`creative_design_voice`, `agents_run_tests`, `agents_compute_kb_rag_index`, `agents_query_knowledge_base_rag` and
`creative_create_brand_kit_from_website`. Everything else on a flow is free to call.

## Pricing

- **Price first only when the user asks what something will cost.** ElevenLabs is the only source of a price; there
  is no rate card to work from. Send the same call with `estimate_only: true` and read the figure that comes back:

  ```json
  { "prompt": "a ceramic mug on marble, morning light", "model_id": "gpt-image-2", "generations_count": 1, "estimate_only": true, "context": "price the mug shot" }
  ```

  ```js
  const priced = await tools.elevenlabs.creative_generate_image({ prompt, model_id: "gpt-image-2", generations_count: 1, estimate_only: true, context: "price the mug shot" })
  ```

  Say the price and what it buys, then make the paid call with the same arguments. An estimate charges nothing, but it
  does create a flow and a node in the workspace, so do not price a call the user did not ask to have priced, and ask
  for one estimate per set of arguments, not per attempt.
- **The figure is for the whole batch**, not for one generation, and it can be fractional.
- **Every paid result carries a cost line.** It states what the result itself reported, such as
  `Credits: 762; 762 credits today.`, or `Credits: not reported; …` when the result reported nothing. Repeat it as it
  is; never turn an estimate or a guess into a charge.
- `generations_count` defaults to **4** for image, video and image editing, and to **2** for speech. Pass `1` unless the
  user asked for options.
- `creative_design_voice` and `agents_run_tests` take no `estimate_only`, so nothing can price them, even on request.
  Say so before calling one, and report the cost line their result carries.
- **Never call a generating tool twice to "retry".** A retry starts and charges a second generation. Poll
  `creative_get_flow_run_status` with the `flow_id` until it reports `all_completed` or `has_failures`.
- The workspace's own credit balance at ElevenLabs is the limit. If the user set a credit cap in this plugin's options,
  a call over it is refused with `SPEND_CAP_REACHED` or `PRICE_UNKNOWN`; pass the refusal's next step on rather than
  working around it.

## Speech

`creative_generate_speech` puts the spoken words in `prompt` — there is no `text` parameter — and needs a `voice_id`
and a `model_id`. Call `creative_list_voices` first; a `voice_id` only ever comes from there or from the user. The
default model is `eleven_multilingual_v2`, or `eleven_v3` when the script has audio tags such as `[whispering]`.
Speech returns two takes by default and each is charged.

## Images and video

`creative_generate_image`, `creative_generate_video` and `creative_edit_image` take `prompt` and `model_id`;
`creative_edit_image` also takes `connect_from`, a node on the same flow. `gemini-2.5-flash-image` is the general
default; `gpt-image-2` for rendered text, infographics and reference-driven edits; `flux-2-pro` for fine detail.
`creative_get_model_guide` explains how to prompt one model, `creative_get_model_schema` gives its parameters, and
`creative_get_flow_node_types` lists what the workspace can run.

## Chaining on one flow

Nodes on different flows cannot be connected. Call `creative_create_flow` first, then pass that `flow_id` to every
related call and wire with `connect_from` (a `node_id` from a tool result or `creative_get_flow`, never invented).
`creative_generate_in_flow` adds and runs a node of a given `node_type`; `creative_run_flow_nodes` re-runs the
`node_ids` you name. Both are charged like any other generation.

## Keeping a file

A result carries a signed link on `elevenlabsusercontent.com` that **expires in about two hours**, plus a canvas `url`
that does not. To keep the file, call `elevenlabs_save_media` with the link:

```json
{ "url": "https://…elevenlabsusercontent.com/…", "name": "intro-voiceover.mp3" }
```

It answers with the path, size, sha256 and, when the container states one, the duration. Files go under the plugin's
`mediaRoot` (status shows it; the default is `~/Downloads/elevenlabs`). Never paste the bytes into the conversation, never
put a generated file in a git repository unless the user asks, and never re-generate to "refresh" an expired link: fetch
the generation again, or open the flow.

## Transcription

`creative_transcribe_audio` transcribes a node already on a flow: it takes `connect_from` and a `model_id`, never a file
or a path from this machine. To transcribe audio that is not on a flow yet, put it there first with
`creative_create_asset_upload` and `creative_finalize_asset_upload`, and say that the audio leaves the machine before
doing it. The transcription itself is charged like a generation.

## Not this skill

Agent settings are the `elevenlabs` skill. What callers said to an agent is `elevenlabs-calls`.

# ElevenLabs agents

Read this before the first `agents_*` call. Every tool takes a `context` parameter: pass one short line naming the user's
goal, with no caller's name, number or words in it.

## Start by reading

`agents_list` to find the agent, then `agents_get` for its configuration. Ids only ever come from a tool result or the
user; never guess or rebuild one. `agents_get` is a read and runs freely:

```js
const found = await tools.elevenlabs.agents_list({ context: "find the checkout agent" })
const agent = await tools.elevenlabs.agents_get({ agent_id: found[0].agent_id, context: "read the checkout agent" })
```

## Changing an agent

`agents_update` **publishes to the live branch immediately**, `main` by default. It is not a draft and this plugin cannot
undo it. So:

- read the agent first, and send only the fields that should change;
- say what will change and that it goes live, in one sentence;
- for anything a caller could notice, prefer `agents_create_branch`, make the change on the branch, then
  `agents_merge_branch_preview` before `agents_merge_branch`.

`agents_duplicate` is usually better than rebuilding a configuration by hand.

## Knowledge base

Add with `agents_create_kb_url` (a page that can keep syncing) or `agents_create_kb_text`; organise with
`agents_create_kb_folder`. Before a delete, check `agents_get_kb_dependents`: other agents may use the document.
`agents_bulk_delete_knowledge_base` is irreversible.

## Tests and deployment

Create a test with `agents_create_test`; inspect past runs with `agents_list_test_runs` and `agents_get_test_run`.
`agents_run_tests` **spends credits**: it makes the agent hold conversations, and ElevenLabs offers no estimate for it,
so say so before running it and report the cost line its result carries. A deployment moves live traffic:
`agents_create_deployment` after a merge, not before.

## Cost

Before a change that switches the model, `agents_calculate_llm_usage` reports what a conversation would cost. Say the
figure and its basis when the user is choosing.

## Deletes

`agents_delete`, `agents_delete_tool`, `agents_delete_phone_number` and `agents_bulk_delete_knowledge_base` cannot be
undone. Say what will be deleted and whom it affects, in one sentence, then make the one call: the plugin asks for
permission at `access: "ask-changes"` and refuses it at `"read-only"`. If the call is declined, nothing changed.

## Not this skill

Call history and transcripts are `elevenlabs-calls`. Generation is `elevenlabs-creative`.

# ElevenLabs for OpenCode Manage the voice and chat agents in your ElevenLabs workspace, review what callers said to them, and generate speech, images and video through ElevenLabs' official MCP server, from OpenCode. Unofficial; not affiliated with ElevenLabs. ElevenLabs is a trademark of Eleven Labs Inc. The icon is ElevenLabs' "11" symbol, unmodified, on a neutral holding shape three times its height, used under [ElevenLabs' brand guidelines](https://elevenlabs.io/brand) only to identify the service this plugin connects to. ## Requirements - OpenCode `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0`. Tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 and 2.2.6. - macOS or Linux. - An ElevenLabs account with a workspace. Generations spend that workspace's credits. ## Install ```sh opencode plugin add github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v0.0.3 ``` Run `opencode reload`, or restart OpenCode, then run `/elevenlabs-status`. Each release has its own tag, and a Git install does not update by itself. To move to a newer release, remove the old entry with `opencode plugin remove github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v0.0.2`, then add the new tag with `opencode plugin add github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v`. Or add the plugin to `opencode.json` instead, with the same spec: ```json { "plugins": [{ "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v0.0.3" }] } ``` The install takes the GitHub release tag. Its commit carries the built `dist/`, so the install runs no build. A new release is a new tag: install it with its own `#v` spec. ## Sign in Run `/connect` and choose **ElevenLabs**. In the terminal, press `o` or Enter to open the link; on the command line, `opencode mcp auth elevenlabs` opens the browser itself and `opencode auth login elevenlabs` does the same. Sign in with your account, choose the workspace, and approve the permissions the consent screen lists. No API key is copied anywhere, and no client ID ships with the plugin: ElevenLabs accepts a client metadata document, so OpenCode registers itself with the consent screen. Revoke the connection at any time from OpenCode, or from your ElevenLabs account settings. The consent is for seven scopes: `convai_read`, `convai_write`, `text_to_speech`, `speech_history_read`, `flows`, `image_video_generation` and `voice_generation`. ElevenLabs also advertises `ads_read`; this plugin never asks for it, because it has no advertising tool. ## Use Ask for what you want in your own words: - "List my agents and tell me which ones still use the default first message." - "My checkout agent fails when someone asks about refunds. Read yesterday's calls and tell me why." - "Duplicate the production agent, change the voice, and set the first message to Spanish." - "Price a five-second video of a ceramic mug in morning light, tell me what it costs, then make it." - "Save that voiceover to my Downloads folder." One tool and one guard do more than relay ElevenLabs: - **`elevenlabs_save_media`** writes a generated file to disk from the signed link a generation returns. The link expires about two hours after the generation, so this is how a result is kept. It answers with the path, size, sha256 and, when the file states one, the duration; the file itself never enters the conversation. - **a spending guard** adds a cost line to every paid result. It prices a call first and refuses one that does not fit only when you set a credit cap. A script can call the same tools with no model, under the same spending guard: ```sh opencode api post /api/rpc/elevenlabs.tools/agents_list -H "x-opencode-directory:$PWD" -d '{"input":{"sessionID":"ses_…","input":{"context":"list my agents"}}}' ``` [docs/scripting.md](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs/blob/HEAD/docs/scripting.md) has the envelope, the estimate path and every refusal. `/elevenlabs-status` prints the connection, the account, the region, the spend, the tools and one next step. `/elevenlabs` opens the same report in a dialog. `/elevenlabs-doctor` makes the live checks a status report cannot. ## Spending Generations are billed in **credits** against the workspace you signed in with. - **There is no credit cap unless you set one.** ElevenLabs already refuses a call the workspace's balance cannot pay for, and the permission rules decide whether a paid call runs at all: under `access: "ask-changes"` every generation asks, and under `"read-only"` it is denied. With the default options the plugin refuses, cuts and queues nothing for money and sends no estimate before a paid call. Each paid result's cost line says what the result reported, or `Credits: not reported`; it never shows a guess. To know a price first, ask for it: an `estimate_only` call. - **Caps are opt-in.** Set `sessionCreditCap`, `dailyCreditCap` or both to a whole number of credits to add a bound of your own, counted over a rolling 24 hours across sessions, scripts and restarts. While either is set, a generation that does not fit is refused **before it is sent**, a request for more variations than the budget affords is cut to what fits, and the rest of this section's refusals apply. - **How far a cap reaches.** Every hold and every charge is written to this data directory's store under its own key, which only the OpenCode that created it ever rewrites, and a total is read by scanning those keys and adding them up. Nothing merges two writers' records, so no writer can drop another's charge. What a cap cannot do is decide across two running OpenCodes at once: `ctx.storage` has no compare-and-set and no lock, so each admits a call against what it has read. Exactly: **within one OpenCode the caps are exact; across OpenCodes a cap is crossed by at most one call's reservation for each one deciding before its read of the others' holds lands, so eight of them at 3,000 credits a call can spend 31,000 against a 10,000 cap; every OpenCode reads the store behind each call it admits and every five seconds besides, so none decides on a book older than that; a settled charge is never lost.** The crossing needs overlap: calls that wait for one another see one another, and those same eight, run one after the next, spend only the 9,000 that fits. Size a cap as the bound you can afford to be crossed once per extra OpenCode, not as a hard limit on the account. Two machines share nothing: the store cannot see them. - **Every price comes from ElevenLabs, never from this plugin.** There is no rate table here: no credits per character, per second or per minute, and nothing measures a file on this machine. A price is ElevenLabs' answer to the **same call with `estimate_only: true`**: you or the model can ask for one at any time, and while a cap is set the plugin asks for one itself before each paid call. Twelve tools can spend: `creative_generate_speech`, `creative_generate_image`, `creative_generate_video`, `creative_edit_image`, `creative_generate_in_flow`, `creative_run_flow_nodes`, `creative_transcribe_audio`, `creative_design_voice`, `agents_run_tests`, `agents_compute_kb_rag_index`, `agents_query_knowledge_base_rag` and `creative_create_brand_kit_from_website`. The first seven take `estimate_only`; the other five do not, so they run unpriced, and while a cap you set is on they are refused instead. The last three are counted as spending because ElevenLabs' catalogue says neither way and the work they describe — embedding a document, running a RAG query, reading a website — is work it plausibly bills, so each gets a cost line and, under a cap, counts against it. - **An estimate is free, but it is not nothing.** Measured against a real workspace: two estimates moved the balance by zero credits, and each left a flow and a node behind in the workspace. That is why none is sent without a cap. Under a cap, one estimate is asked per set of arguments, the figure is kept for ten minutes, and the paid call reuses it instead of creating a second flow. The estimate is sent only where the paid call could run: the permission it asks for is the generation's own, so nothing is estimated if you say no, and under `access: "read-only"` every spending tool is denied and no estimate is sent either. The plugin raises that permission twice for one paid call — before the estimate, and again for the generation — so under `ask-changes` you may be prompted twice. Whether OpenCode folds the two into one prompt is OpenCode's to decide, and no release has measured it yet. - **The figure is the whole batch.** ElevenLabs answers for every generation the call asks for, not for one — a four-image estimate came back as 761.5151418103446 credits, about 190 an image. Credits are charged as whole numbers, so a fractional figure is rounded up. Under a cap, a batch that does not fit is cut to the number of generations the budget affords, and a call that named no count is refused whole rather than quietly given a smaller batch. - **With no cap, nothing is priced first and nothing is refused.** A cost line reads `Credits: not reported` unless the result reports a figure. **With a cap, a call that cannot be priced is refused, not guessed.** Only when you set a cap: each of the 12 tools that can spend is priced by ElevenLabs' own estimate or refused PRICE_UNKNOWN before it is sent, and so is any name this table does not classify, whatever it starts with. A failed or missing estimate, an argument ElevenLabs' own schema for that tool does not have, and a tool with no estimate at all each end there. The refusal says what to do: send the same call with `estimate_only: true`, or set both caps to `null`. A price of 0 is a refusal, not a free call. - **Transcription spends like everything else.** `creative_transcribe_audio` transcribes a node on a flow — it takes no file and no path — and it is priced from its own estimate. A call that fails, or whose result never arrives, is charged the reserved price: the plugin cannot tell a free failure from a billed one, and over-counting is the safe side. A later result that reports a higher figure may replace that charge. A missing result, a zero, or an error does not free the budget. A hold still open after ten minutes is settled at the reserved price rather than dropped. On the script path, one priced call per session and method is in flight; a second is refused until the first settles. With no cap none of this holds anything back: calls run side by side and each is recorded when its result arrives. - **Past a thousand priced calls in a day, the oldest ones are counted by the hour.** The detail log keeps the newest 1,000 charges; an older charge still inside the window is folded into a total for its session and the hour it was spent in, which nothing afterwards can shrink. # Fixtures

## `live-tools.json`

**Captured from a live account.** It is one raw MCP `tools/list` response, exactly as ElevenLabs' hosted server sent
it: `{ "tools": [ { name, description, inputSchema } ] }`, 190 tools, with their real descriptions, argument names,
defaults and enums. The only edits are redactions: an id-like string inside a description or an example is replaced
with `<prefix>_example`, and nothing but the input schemas is kept.

The host exposes no MCP `annotations` — none of the 190 carries one — so a tool's class cannot be confirmed from the
server and is decided by `classify()` in `src/elevenlabs-tools.ts` from the name, the description and the schema.

`npm run drift` compares the plugin's table with this file: it names every tool the file has and the table does not,
every tool the table has and the file does not, and every class an annotation would contradict if one existed.

## Releasing

Each release is the GitHub tag `v<version>`, where `<version>` is the `version` in `package.json`, and users install from
that tag. The release is one commit on top of a `master` head that CI passed, and the tag points at it. The release
workflow makes both, in GitHub Actions: nobody builds, commits or tags a release on their own machine, and no personal
key signs it.

While changes land, their notes go under `## [Unreleased]` at the top of `CHANGELOG.md`. Each earlier GitHub release is
a `## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD` heading below it, newest first, and the npm history stays last, under
`## Earlier releases on npm`.

1. On `master`, set `version` in `package.json` to the new version, and change every install spec in the README,
   `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/` to `#v<version>` (`test/docs.test.ts` fails until they match). Then run
   `node scripts/changelog.mjs release`: it turns `## [Unreleased]` into `## [<version>] - <today>`, above the earlier
   releases, and refuses a CHANGELOG it cannot shape. Run `npm run check`.
2. Push that commit to `master`, and wait for CI to pass on it.
3. Start the release with that commit's full sha:
   `gh workflow run release.yml --ref master -f sha=<full sha>`, or from Actions → release →
   Run workflow, on `master`.
4. Read the run's summary, then approve the `release` environment. The summary is on the run page, under the `stage`
   job: the tag, the parent and its CI run, the release commit and its tree, the sha256 of `SHA256SUMS` and the staged
   artifact's id, `SHA256SUMS` itself, and the notes. Open the release commit on `release/v<version>` and read them
   before approving: the approval releases exactly those bytes. Only the owner approves a release. Agents never approve
   one, never call the deployment-approval API, and never bypass a ruleset or the environment; the kit's scripts make
   only their own GitHub calls and refuse every other.
5. Check the published Release: not a draft, its notes, and every asset against `SHA256SUMS`.

Before the approval, the workflow:
- **plans:** refuses a run that is not on `master`, a sha that is not `master`'s head, a sha without a successful `ci.yml`
  push run, a version that is not `x.y.z`, a CHANGELOG whose newest release is not this version, a release that does not
  move forward from the last published Release, a leftover `release/v<version>` branch, a native run that did not build
  this sha on `master`, by hand, with success, and a missing `native_run` (or one given to a plugin that is not native);
- **builds** `dist/` with `npm ci --ignore-scripts` and `npm run build`, with a read-only token, and writes the release
  files: `dist/`, `package.json` without its lifecycle scripts, and the vetted native manifest;
- **commits** them on a temporary branch `release/v<version>` at the parent, through GitHub's API with the workflow's token,
  so GitHub signs the commit (author `github-actions[bot]`, committer GitHub). This job runs no npm. It refuses a commit
  that GitHub does not verify, or whose parent or tree is not the one the files give;
- **verifies** on a fresh runner: the commit's identity, one parent on `master`, `package.json` exactly the parent's
  without the lifecycle scripts, only regular files in the allowed paths, no `package.json` under `dist/`, and a second,
  independent build of the parent (its own job) equal to the committed `dist/` byte for byte;
- **installs** the release commit with `plugin add` on each stock OpenCode host (2.2.3 to 2.2.6);
- **packs** the commit before installing anything and keeps that tarball, then runs the pack stage against a copy;
- **stages** the Release: verifies the attested native files, writes `SHA256SUMS` and the notes (the version's CHANGELOG
  section), and shows them all in the run summary with the sha256 of `SHA256SUMS`.

A job either runs repository or dependency code (`npm ci`, the build, the pack stage, a host install) and has no write
token, or uses the API and runs only the kit's scripts on a fresh checkout, after checking that the release commit's
`scripts/` and `.github/` are the parent's. The first kind is not token-free: `actions/checkout` fetches with the job's
read-only (`contents: read`) token, and its post step and the artifact uploads run after repository code on the same
runner, so that code could reach a read-only token for this public repository and the runner's artifact token. Jobs
pass files as artifacts downloaded by the id the uploading job gave, and each is checked again on arrival.

After the approval, it downloads the staged artifact by the id the summary names, and refuses unless `SHA256SUMS` has
the sha256 the summary shows and every staged file matches it, and every native file is the one the release commit's
`manifest/native.json` pins, size and sha256, with each gzip holding the pinned executable. Then it checks everything again, creates the annotated tag
`v<version>` on the release commit (tagger `github-actions[bot]`, unsigned), checks the tag, creates the Release with the
notes, the tarball, the native files and `SHA256SUMS`, and deletes `release/v<version>`. The tag keeps the commit.

GitHub's signature and the bot identity show only that GitHub made the commit through its API for the workflow; anyone
with write access can make such a commit. What ties the release to `master` is its content: one parent CI passed, the
exact `package.json`, the allowed paths and the byte-for-byte rebuild. Never relax those because the commit is signed.

**A rejected, expired or failed run** leaves nothing behind: the `cleanup` job deletes `release/v<version>` when it points
at the parent or at that run's commit, and never touches another branch. No tag exists before the approval, so the
version is not burned: fix `master` and start again. If `cleanup` itself failed, the next run refuses until the branch
is deleted: `gh api -X DELETE repos/joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs/git/refs/heads/release/v<version>`.

**Resume.** If the run fails after creating the tag and before the Release is complete, start it again with the same `sha`. The plan finds the kit's tag on a release commit on that sha with no published Release, and resumes:
it makes no new commit, checks and installs the tagged commit, stages the files, and after a new approval reuses the tag
and adds what the Release lacks. Delete a draft Release a failed upload left first: the publish step refuses a draft.
Any other existing tag is refused: release the next version.

The repository's tag ruleset keeps a `v*` tag from being moved or deleted. A stray `v*` tag, one that never became a
Release, does not block later releases: only published Releases count, and drafts do not. Its version cannot be
released, so release the next one. To remove the tag anyway, an admin disables the `release tags` ruleset, deletes the
tag, and restores the ruleset exactly as it was.

**Known limit: a `v*` tag pushed by hand.** No ruleset limits who creates a `v*` tag, so anyone with write access can
push one by hand, pointing at any commit. Such a tag has no published Release, the forward-only check ignores it, and
Jelly installs only a published Release whose `SHA256SUMS` it verifies. But a user who installs
`github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v<x>` directly gets whatever that tag points at. Only the release workflow makes
release tags; never push one by hand.

The release kit is these files, the same in every plugin: `scripts/release-rules.mjs`, `scripts/release-commit.mjs`,
`scripts/release-github.mjs`, `scripts/check-release-shape.mjs`, `scripts/changelog.mjs`, `scripts/release-version.mjs`,
`scripts/release-pack.mjs`, `scripts/publish-release.mjs`, `scripts/attach-native.mjs`, `scripts/native-manifest.mjs`,
`scripts/tested-hosts.mjs`, `scripts/check-release-plugin-add.sh`, `scripts/release-kit.test.mjs` and
`.github/workflows/release.yml`. Do not re-run the older `apply-release-kit.mjs`: it writes back the kit that could
release only `v0.0.0`.

Each release has its own tag, and a Git install does not update by itself. To move to a newer release, remove the old entry with `opencode plugin remove github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v<old version>`, then add the new tag with `opencode plugin add github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v<version>`.

Or add the plugin to `opencode.json` instead, with the same spec:

```json
{ "plugins": [{ "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v0.0.3" }] }
```

## Data handling

- **The OAuth token is OpenCode's.** The plugin never reads, stores, logs or prints it; the MCP transport and every
  refresh are OpenCode's. Nothing the plugin writes contains a token, an authorization code or a signed link's query.
- **Transcripts are other people's personal data.** `agents_get_conversation` returns a caller's words, the identifier
  your integration gave them, the phone number they called from, whatever the agent extracted, and the variables their
  app passed in. It lands in the model's context and in the session history on disk. There is no redaction: the point of
  reading a call is what was said. `conversations: "summary"` denies the words and keeps the metadata; `"off"` denies the
  history too. The match ignores case. `"off"` denies a name containing `conversation` or `transcript`, a name containing
  `call` and `recording`, and the shapes `get_call`, `list_calls` and `export_history`. It does not deny a generation or
  a transcription: those names do not match. `"summary"` denies the transcript tools and the transcript patterns.
- **Generated files stay on your disk.** `elevenlabs_save_media` writes under `mediaRoot` and returns a path, a size, a
  sha256 and, when the container states one, a duration. The bytes never enter the conversation, and nothing is
  uploaded anywhere.
- **The optional API key** is stored by OpenCode's credential store, is used for one read (`GET /v1/user/subscription`),
  and is never printed: not in status, not in an error, not in a log. Remove it in `/connect` at any time.
- **Nothing is sent anywhere else.** The plugin's only outbound requests are the media download you ask for and that
  subscription read; the doctor fetches ElevenLabs' own discovery documents. What the *model* sends to ElevenLabs is a
  separate matter: its tool calls go to ElevenLabs' own server, and one of those tools, `get_more_tools`, exists to
  carry a free-text sentence the model wrote itself. See Permissions below.
- **Redaction.** Text from OpenCode or the network is cut to one line, at most 160 characters, with URL credentials,
  queries and fragments removed and token shapes replaced, before it reaches status, the dialog or the session.

## Permissions

**Every tool is allowed by default.** With `access: "all"` an agent can, without asking:

- **Spend your credits.** Twelve tools bill the workspace you signed in with: speech, images, video, image editing,
  generating inside a flow, running a flow's nodes, transcription, voice design, running an agent test, indexing a
  knowledge-base document, running a RAG query, and building a brand kit from a website. The last three are counted as
  spending because ElevenLabs' catalogue says neither way and each describes work it plausibly bills; silence is read
  against your money rather than for it. An image or
  video call returns **four variations by default** and speech returns **two takes**, so one call can be four billable
  generations, and asking for a retry starts and charges another. **Transcription bills too**, and it is a *change*,
  not a read: `access: "read-only"` denies it along with every other tool that can spend. Every paid result carries a
  cost line with the figure the result reported, or `Credits: not reported`. **No credit cap is set by default**, and
  then no estimate is sent before a paid call: the bounds are the workspace's balance at ElevenLabs and the permission rules (`ask-changes` asks
  for every paid call, `read-only` denies it, and a script's `ask` is refused). The caps (`sessionCreditCap`,
  `dailyCreditCap`) are opt-in; once set, the plugin asks ElevenLabs for an estimate of each paid call, reserves it
  before the call and bounds this plugin, not your account. Five of the twelve have no estimate — `creative_design_voice`, `agents_run_tests`,
  `agents_compute_kb_rag_index`, `agents_query_knowledge_base_rag` and `creative_create_brand_kit_from_website` — so
  they run unpriced, and while a cap you set is on they are refused instead.
- **An estimate is a call of its own.** Without a cap the plugin sends none; one the model or a script asks for is theirs. It costs nothing — measured against a real workspace, two of them moved the
  balance by zero — but each one creates a flow and a node in the workspace. Under a cap, the plugin asks for one per set of
  arguments, keeps it for ten minutes, and sends it only where the paid call is permitted: the permission it asks for
  is the generation's own, never one of its own, and under `read-only` nothing is estimated because nothing may be
  generated. That permission is raised twice for one paid call — before the estimate and again for the generation — so
  under `ask-changes` expect up to two prompts. Earlier releases promised one; whether a host folds them has never been
  measured here.
- **What a cap cannot decide.** Exactly: **within one OpenCode the caps are exact; across OpenCodes a cap is crossed
  by at most one call's reservation for each one deciding before its read of the others' holds lands, so eight of them
  at 3,000 credits a call can spend 31,000 against a 10,000 cap; every OpenCode reads the store behind each call it
  admits and every five seconds besides, so none decides on a book older than that; a settled charge is never lost.**
  The crossing needs overlap: calls that wait for one another see one another, and those same eight, run one after the
  next, spend only the 9,000 that fits. A cap is not a
  lock: `ctx.storage` offers `get`, `set`, `remove` and `scan`, and no compare-and-set, so two OpenCodes running at once
  on one data directory each admit against what they have read. Nothing is lost to that race, because every hold and
  every charge has its own key that only its own OpenCode rewrites and a total is a scan and a sum, not a merge. The
  check and the hold are taken in memory with nothing awaited between them, so two calls in one process cannot both
  pass; the hold's key is then written and awaited before the call is dispatched, and a write that fails refuses the
  call. Set the caps with the bound you can afford to be crossed once per extra OpenCode, not as a hard limit on the
  account; the account's own limits are at ElevenLabs. A cap also binds one server entry: the `elevenlabs` entry this plugin manages. A second MCP
  entry pointing at ElevenLabs under another name serves its tools under that name's prefix, which this plugin's hooks
  never see, so its calls are priced by nothing here. `/elevenlabs-status` names such an entry when one exists.
- **Change live agents.** `agents_update` publishes straight to the branch it targets, `main` by default. It is not
  staged as a draft, and the plugin cannot undo it. A prompt edit changes what a production agent says to real callers on
  the next call.
- **Delete permanently.** `agents_delete`, `agents_delete_tool`, `agents_delete_phone_number` and
  `agents_bulk_delete_knowledge_base` cannot be reversed.
- **Publish and deploy.** `agents_create_deployment` moves live traffic; `agents_duplicate` and `agents_create_branch`
  create entities that can be deployed.
- **Grant access from outside.** `agents_get_link` mints a shareable link; anyone with it can use the agent or the test
  session.
- **Read callers' calls.** Every transcript and its extracted fields, as above.
- **Send your audio to ElevenLabs.** The reference-file and asset-upload tools send what you point them at.
  `creative_transcribe_audio` does not: it takes no file and no path, and transcribes a node already on a flow in the
  workspace. No price in this plugin reads a file on this machine.
- **Write outside the project.** `elevenlabs_save_media` writes under `mediaRoot`. It asserts both its own action and
  OpenCode's `external_directory` rule for that folder before it fetches anything, so a session that denies
  `external_directory` writes nothing.
- **Ask ElevenLabs to build new tools, in words the model writes itself.** `get_more_tools` takes one free-text
  argument, `capability`, and ElevenLabs uses it to decide which tools get built next. It is the one tool that carries
  a sentence the model composed out of the workspace. It carries no workspace data, returns no tool and adds nothing at
  run time, but under `access: "all"` it goes out without a prompt. `ask-changes` asks for it; `read-only` denies it.
- **Use a tool ElevenLabs adds later.** The `elevenlabs_*` rule allows it, and status names it as unknown. With no
  credit cap, the default, it runs unpriced. While a cap you set is on it cannot spend unpriced: a name this release
  does not classify is refused `PRICE_UNKNOWN` before it is sent, whatever it is called — the money gate is the tool
  table, not a name prefix. A new deleting tool still runs until it is classified,
  because permission is a separate axis from money: `ask-changes` and `read-only` are what bound it.

One line restricts all of it: set `"access": "ask-changes"` (reads run, everything else asks) or `"access": "read-only"`
(reads run, everything else is denied), or add a rule for one tool, such as
`{ "action": "elevenlabs_agents_delete", "resource": "*", "effect": "deny" }`.

In an unattended run such as `opencode run`, a tool that asks is refused rather than left waiting.

## Scripts

The tools RPC, `elevenlabs.tools`, lets a script call the same tools with no model, under the same spending guard. A
script runs as the agent of the session it names, so it gets the same default: with `access: "all"` it can make every
call above, spending credits included. To restrict a script, set `access` to `"ask-changes"` or `"read-only"`, or add a
rule to its agent or session. A script never waits on a prompt: an ask is refused, and a saved "Always allow" approval
does not authorize a script. [docs/scripting.md](https://github.com/joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs/blob/HEAD/docs/scripting.md)
has the envelope and every refusal.

# Architecture

The plugin is a thin layer over ElevenLabs' hosted MCP server. OpenCode owns the MCP transport, OAuth, credentials,
permission prompts and tool output limits. The plugin registers the server, names its `/connect` entry, adds the default
permission rules, guards spending, saves generated files, reports status, ships three skills, and lets scripts call the
known tools through a tools RPC. It adds one tool of its own and has no runtime dependencies beyond Node's built-ins.

## Setup

1. `parseOptions` validates the options; anything wrong fails with `OPTIONS_INVALID`.
2. `checkHost` compares `ctx.app.version` with `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0`. Inside it the plugin starts; status calls only 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5 and 2.2.6 tested. Outside it, setup fails with `HOST_UNTESTED` unless `allowUntestedHost` is set.
3. The ledger is read from `ctx.storage` once, so the 24-hour total survives a reload.
4. `ctx.mcp.transform` registers `elevenlabs` at the selected region's URL, with `oauth.scope` pinned to seven scopes, or
   adopts the user's own entry at exactly that URL. Another region's URL is `stale`; any other is `conflict`.
5. `ctx.tool.transform` sets the namespace description and adds `elevenlabs_save_media`.
6. `ctx.agent.transform` inserts the default rules after each agent's base `* * allow`.
7. `ctx.integration.transform` adds the optional API key entry to `/connect`.
8. `ctx.skill.transform`, `ctx.command.transform` (`/elevenlabs-status`, `/elevenlabs-doctor`) and `ctx.rpc.register`
   (`elevenlabs/status`).
9. `registerToolsRpc` registers `elevenlabs.tools` with the spending guard's shapers.
10. `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before")` prices a spending call from ElevenLabs' own estimate, may cut a `generations_count`
    the caller named to what the budget affords, and refuses a call that does not fit before it is sent.
    `ctx.tool.hook("execute.after")` charges the ledger and appends the cost line, and the expiry line for a
    generation's link. An `estimate_only` call is neither priced nor charged: its answer is remembered as the price of
    the paid call with the same arguments.
11. `watchIntegration` starts. Setup returns one cleanup that stops it, both hooks and the tools RPC.

Transforms are synchronous and never throw: a failure is kept as a problem for status, and cleared when the next replay
succeeds.

## Platform facts (OpenCode 2.2.3 to 2.2.6)

- **The sign-in is CIMD.** ElevenLabs' authorization server advertises `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true` and
  no registration endpoint, so OpenCode sends its own client metadata document
  (`https://opencode.ai/oauth/opencode/client.json`). Nothing ships with the plugin. A pinned `client_id` or
  `redirect_uri` would disable that; the plugin pins neither.
- **The scope pin.** OpenCode requests `oauth.scope` when it is set, otherwise the scope in the `401` challenge
  (ElevenLabs' names none), otherwise every scope in `scopes_supported`. ElevenLabs advertises eight; the plugin pins the
  seven its own MCP client asks for, so `ads_read` is never requested. A host test asserts the exact scopes in the
  authorization request and fails if the pin is removed.
- **Discovery.** The global MCP resource names `https://api.us.elevenlabs.io` as its authorization server, so the global
  and US servers share one. Each region serves the same documents with its own host, and each accepts CIMD.
- **The token never reaches the plugin.** OpenCode holds it and refreshes it; `/elevenlabs-status` sees only a
  credential's label. That is why the balance needs a separate key.
- **The hooks.** `execute.before` can change an MCP call's arguments on the model path and in Code Mode, and
  `execute.after` can add to a result. The tools RPC's executor bypasses both, so the same guard runs there through the
  block's own shapers.
- **A plugin tool's declared permission only hides it on a deny.** Every plugin-owned tool that writes asserts its own
  action inside `execute`; `elevenlabs_save_media` does, on both paths.
- **Changing a server's URL changes its integration id** (`mcp_` + `sha1(name\0url)`), so a region change needs a new
  sign-in and leaves the old credential behind. Status detects that and gives one next step.
- **`dist/tui.js` carries no zod and no host contract**: the RPC contract is plain JSON Schema, written with
  `Rpc.define`.

## The spending guard

**ElevenLabs is the only source of a price.** This plugin computes none of its own: no rate per character, per second
or per minute, and no measurement of a local file. A call that can spend is priced by sending ElevenLabs the same call
with `estimate_only: true` and the same arguments, and reading the figure out of its answer (`estimatePrice` in
`src/billing.ts`). `ESTIMATE_TOOLS` holds the seven tools whose live schema declares `estimate_only`; `SPEND_TOOLS`
holds the twelve that can spend. A spending tool with no estimate — `creative_design_voice`, `agents_run_tests`,
`agents_compute_kb_rag_index`, `agents_query_knowledge_base_rag` and `creative_create_brand_kit_from_website` — has no
price at all: with no cap it runs unpriced, and while a cap the owner set is on it is refused (`PRICE_UNKNOWN`).

**Caps are opt-in.** `sessionCreditCap` and `dailyCreditCap` default to `null`. With neither set, `quote` and
`quoteSync` send no estimate and refuse, clamp and reserve nothing. Each path records the figure the result itself
reports, or reports `Credits: not reported`. The script path keeps nothing between calls: with no call id on
`ShapeCall` it could not pair a result with its call, so it does not try, and it tells an `estimate_only` answer from a
paid result by the answer's own `estimate` object (`isEstimateResult`). Everything below about refusals, clamps, holds and the one-in-flight rule applies only while a cap is
set. The bounds without one are ElevenLabs' own balance check and the permission rules.

**The figure is read strictly.** `estimatedCreditsOf` reads `estimate.credits` first, because that is the field the
live result used (`{"estimate": {"credits": 761.5151418103446}}`), then the same five named keys settlement reads a
charge under, at the top level. Nothing is read out of prose, and nothing is walked for several levels: a figure this
parser does not find leaves the call with no price, which a cap, when set, turns into `PRICE_UNKNOWN`. The estimate sets the
reservation and, where no later figure is seen, the charge, so it is read under at least the rules a figure that could
*lower* a reservation is read under.

The figure ElevenLabs answers with is the **batch total** for the call it was sent, which live reconcile 1 measured: an
estimate for four images came back as 761.5151418103446 credits, about 190 each. It is often fractional, and a
fractional estimate is a real figure — the ledger rounds it up (`Math.ceil`) and the cost line names the figure it
rounded from. When the call states no count, the batch is the server's own default for that tool
(`GENERATION_DEFAULTS`: four for an image or an image edit, two for speech, one for a video), so a price divided per
generation is divided by that default and the cost line says so. A tool whose schema declares `generations_count` with
no default of its own — `creative_generate_in_flow`, `creative_run_flow_nodes` — gets no per-generation figure, only
the total.

**An estimate is free but not harmless.** Live reconcile 1 measured two of them against the workspace balance and saw
no movement and no new billable request, and each one created a flow and a node in the owner's workspace. So with no
cap the guard sends none at all, and under a cap it asks for one estimate per set of arguments, remembers the figure for ten minutes (`RESERVATION_MS`), and reuses it for
the paid call rather than creating a second flow. Different arguments are a different call and get their own estimate.

**The estimate is asked for only where the paid call could run.** `estimatorFor` asserts the paid tool's own permission
(`elevenlabs_<tool>`, through `ctx.permission.assert`) before it sends anything — never a permission of its own, so
nothing can be estimated that the generation itself may not do. Under `access: "ask-changes"` the estimate goes out
only if that permission is allowed, so an estimate never creates a flow for a generation the user is about to refuse.
Under `access: "read-only"` every spending tool is denied, the assert fails, and no estimate is sent either. A declined
or failed assert leaves the call with no price, which a cap, when set, turns into `PRICE_UNKNOWN`.

**How many prompts the user sees is the host's, and is not yet measured (RE-8).** Two asserts are raised for one priced
call: `estimatorFor`'s, before the estimate, and the generation's own when it runs. `test/unit/regressions-6.test.ts`
counts them, so the number cannot change unnoticed. Whether OpenCode turns two asserts into one prompt — by holding an
"allow once" answer for the same action within the same tool call — cannot be established without a host, and no
version of this plugin has measured it. Earlier releases of these docs said the user is "asked once"; that was a claim
about what a host does, written as though this plugin decided it. Live pass 2 counts the prompts under `ask-changes`.
The ordering itself is settled and is the safe one: asserting before estimating is what keeps `read-only` from creating
a flow, and what makes `ask-changes` refuse the estimate when the generation is refused.

While a cap the owner set is on, two kinds of call are priced or refused before dispatch: the ones the table classifies as
spending, and **any name the table does not classify at all, whatever it starts with**. There is no keyword list and
no prefix. A price that does not fit is refused (`SPEND_CAP_REACHED`), and a count the caller named is first cut to
what the budget affords; a call that named no count is refused at its whole figure rather than quietly given a smaller
batch than it asked for.

The unknown half is what closes the chain that starts at `get_more_tools`: a tool asks ElevenLabs to build more tools,
and a tool this release has never seen has no schema to check its arguments against and no `estimate_only` flag to
call, so nothing here could price it. A read the table already classifies still runs without a price, as it always
did, and so does the plugin's own `elevenlabs_save_media`.

Each refusal names what it could not price and what to do about it, in three shapes. A tool that takes `estimate_only`
is told to send the same call with `estimate_only: true` first. A classified spending tool that does not —
`creative_design_voice` and `agents_run_tests` — is told that ElevenLabs offers no estimate for it and that both caps
must be `null` to run it. A name the table does not know is told that nothing here can tell whether it spends, and to
set both caps to `null` or wait for a release that classifies it.

A price is **reserved** in the ledger before the call is sent and settled into a charge when its result arrives, so a
parallel turn cannot spend one budget twice. A call that fails, and a hold still open after ten minutes, is charged the
reserved price: the plugin cannot tell a free failure from a billed one. A later higher figure may replace that charge.
A zero or a missing result does not free the budget. A charge stays in the session that reserved it, whichever session
a later result is delivered under, exactly as it keeps that row's figure as its floor: a settlement may raise what a
call cost but never moves it to another session's budget. The ledger is append-only: every hold and every charge is one
`ctx.storage` key, `spend/<writerId>/<entryId>`, where `writerId` is unique to this plugin instance and only the
instance that created a key ever rewrites it. A total is a scan over `spend/` and a sum — there is no merge, no
`Math.max` and no read-modify-write of a shared record, so no writer can drop another's row. Pruning folds older
entries into that writer's own hourly key, `spend/<writerId>/h/<hour>`, and the hours of every writer are added
together, which cannot double-count because a charge is folded by exactly one writer. A folded hour is kept while any
minute of its hour is still inside the window, so a folded charge counts for up to an hour past its own day, and never
less than it. A key is removed only once it is past the window. Two ledgers handed one storage object share a book and
one daily cap, as two locations in one OpenCode do. Across processes, exactly: **within one OpenCode the caps are
exact; across OpenCodes a cap is crossed by at most one call's reservation for each one deciding before its read of the
others' holds lands, so eight of them at 3,000 credits a call can spend 31,000 against a 10,000 cap; every OpenCode
reads the store behind each call it admits and every five seconds besides, so none decides on a book older than that; a
settled charge is never lost.** The crossing needs overlap: calls that wait for one another see one another, and those
same eight, run one after the next, spend only the 9,000 that fits.

The bound follows from the order each path works in. `quote` can await, so it refreshes from the store and then
reserves: the most it can admit beyond a cap is one reservation for every OpenCode that read before the first of them
wrote. `quoteSync` cannot await before it dispatches, by the shaper contract, so it bounds its staleness behind itself
instead — it starts a read it does not wait for after the hold is taken, and the next call on that ledger decides from
a book that has seen the other OpenCodes' holds. A process that is idle, or whose calls all refuse, writes nothing and
would never read again, so setup also starts an unref'd timer that reads the store every `LEDGER_REFRESH_MS`, five
seconds, and stops when the plugin is disposed. Measured over one store, 100-credit calls against a 10,000 cap: two
OpenCodes spending together reach 10,000, eight reach 10,400, and an OpenCode that started before another spent the
whole cap admits one call before its next read, or none once the timer has run. Without those two reads the same
measurements were 20,000, 80,000 and a whole fresh cap. `reserve` keeps its check and its hold synchronous, with
nothing awaited between them, then
writes the hold's own key and awaits it before dispatch; a failed write takes the hold back out of memory and refuses
the call. Two machines share nothing. Two locations keep their own tools-RPC shapers. On the script path, one priced
call per session and method is in flight.

### Argument allowlists

Every tool the guard prices has a list of the argument names it may carry while a cap is on, and each list is that
tool's own live schema, name for name, taken from `test/fixtures/live-tools.json` and held against it by
`test/unit/live-schema.test.ts`. An argument outside the list is one ElevenLabs' own schema for that tool does not
have, so the call is refused (`PRICE_UNKNOWN`) and the refusal names the argument. The estimate is not asked for in
that case either: it would answer for arguments nothing here can account for, and leave another flow behind for a call
that is going to be refused. With both caps off nothing is priced and the same call runs. Live reconcile 2 is where
the lists are checked again, by the step that says to confirm each priced tool's real argument names in
`test/fixtures/README.md`.

Every priced call may carry `estimate_only`, `context` and `flow_id`. Every priced call **except a transcription** may also carry
the count key `generations_count`, which is the only batch-size name in the live catalogue — it appears on six tools,
and a count under any other name is an argument the live schema does not have. A transcription takes none: it
transcribes the node it is connected to, once.

| `creative_generate_image`, `creative_generate_video`, `creative_edit_image` | `prompt`, `model_id`, `connect_from` |

The five spending tools with no list are `creative_design_voice`, `agents_run_tests`, `agents_compute_kb_rag_index`,

### What each tool is allowed to do

`classify()` puts each of the 190 live tools in one class, from its own name, description and schema: 81 reads, 2
exports, 81 writes, 12 that can spend and 14 destructive. Nothing is left unclassified. The class is the worst thing a
tool can do; it never decides whether a call runs, only what the generated default rules give it.

Some of them are judgement calls, recorded here because nothing in the catalogue settles them. **One rule decides every
tool the catalogue is silent about:** a tool whose own description says it does server-side work ElevenLabs plausibly
bills, and does not say it spends nothing, is counted as spending. The tools that genuinely do not spend say so
unprompted — `creative_upload_flow_reference` ends *"This starts no generation and spends no credits"*,
`creative_update_node`, `creative_update_flow_nodes` and `creative_duplicate_flow_nodes` each end *"This never starts a
generation"*, `creative_get_voice_design_previews` says it reads previews *"without spending credits"* — so silence
beside billable work is the signal, and a cost line on a call that turns out free is better than a charge nobody
reported. Four tools are classed as spending on that rule and nothing else; none of the four declares `estimate_only`,
so each runs unpriced, or is refused while a cap is set, and live pass 2 measures whether they bill:

- **`agents_run_tests`.** A test run makes the agent hold conversations, which bills the agent's own LLM usage.
  `agents_create_test` and the other test tools only describe a test, and are ordinary writes.
- **`agents_compute_kb_rag_index`.** It starts RAG indexing of a knowledge-base document for an embedding model:
  embedding a whole document is server-side work with a unit ElevenLabs could bill.
- **`agents_query_knowledge_base_rag`.** A RAG query embeds the query and searches the index. It was classed a read
  until this release, which made the table hold two standards for the same silence: this is the read whose own
  description names the same kind of work `agents_compute_kb_rag_index` does.
- **`creative_create_brand_kit_from_website`.** It fetches a public website and extracts its logo, colours,
  typography and tone — *"best-effort and takes a while"*, which is the shape of a billed extraction.
- **`creative_design_voice` is counted as spending** and `creative_save_designed_voice` is a write: designing previews
  is the part that generates audio.
- **`creative_create_asset_upload` is a write, not an export.** It opens an upload into the workspace; nothing leaves
  it. The two exports are `agents_get_link`, which mints a link usable outside the workspace, and
  `creative_get_generations`, which returns the signed links a flow's generations can be downloaded from.
- **`creative_show_flow_results` is a write, not a read.** It returns a run's generations, but what it *does* is
  *"put a run's generations back in front of the user, rendering the same view a run starts with"*. The catalogue
  draws the line itself: `creative_get_flow_run_status` returns the same data and says *"without showing anything to
  the user — this never renders a view"*. Rendering something to the user is an effect, so the class follows what the
  call does rather than what it returns, and `read-only` no longer lets a session push a view into the workspace.
  It spends nothing and is not priced.

- **`get_more_tools` is a write.** It is not a catalogue pager and it returns no tool definitions. Its live schema has
  one required argument, a free-text string named `capability`, and its description says what the server does with it:
  *"Call this when the user's request cannot be completed with any of the available tools. Describe the capability you
  were looking for, so it can inform which tools get built next."* So it changes what ElevenLabs will offer, which is a
  change like any other, and it is the one tool that sends words the model composed itself out of the workspace. It
  asks under `ask-changes`, `read-only` denies it, and SECURITY.md lists it with the other things `access: "all"`
  allows without a prompt. This release classified it from its own schema after live reconcile 1; until then the table
  held it unclassified and described it as something it never was.

Nothing is left unclassified, so `/elevenlabs-status` reports `0 unknown` against this catalogue. A name that really
fits no class would go in `UNCLASSIFIED_TOOLS`, where `npm run drift` reports it as known rather than as drift — but
while a credit cap the owner set is on, a name the table does not classify is refused before dispatch, so holding one
there is not free.

### The one duration, and what it is not

`elevenlabs_save_media` prints how long a saved file is. Nothing else in the plugin reads a file's length, and no
price comes from one.

It used to. Until live reconcile 1 the guard priced a transcription by measuring the local WAV it was given, at a
per-minute rate written down here. The live catalogue ended that: `creative_transcribe_audio` takes no file and no
path — its arguments are `connect_from`, `flow_id`, `model_id`, `view_state_id`, `context` and `estimate_only` — so
the audio it bills for is a node on a flow in the workspace, and the server never opens anything on this disk. A
duration measured here would have answered for a file ElevenLabs was not charging for. Transcription is now priced
the way every other spending call is, from ElevenLabs' own estimate, and the whole of the measuring apparatus the old
price rested on — the stamping of each file's device, inode, size and modification time before and after the
measurement, the freezing of the arguments that named them, the refusal of a file that moved between the two
readings — went with it. There is no local file in a price to protect.

What remains is `durationOf`, and it is a display figure. The saved line reads a PCM RIFF/WAVE file the way a decoder
does — the `fmt ` fields and the bytes behind `data` — and otherwise reads the duration an MP4 or M4A states in the
`mvhd` box inside its `moov`, which is the format ElevenLabs returns and carries no length a decoder-free reader
could compute. That walk is bounded: every read is inside the file's own size, the number of boxes it steps through
is capped, and a stated duration longer than the file's bytes could hold at 8 kbps is dropped rather than shown. A
file whose length depends on which decoder opens it — two `data` chunks, which CoreAudio and Python's `wave` read
differently, or two `fmt ` chunks, which are two sample rates and so two lengths — carries no duration on the saved
line at all. A `data` size that understates the bytes behind it is reported at the longer reading, with
`understated` saying so, so a line that disagrees with the owner's own player can be explained.

The rigour is kept because a figure shown to the owner should be one a decoder would agree with. It is not kept
because anything depends on it: `savedText` prints `Saved <mime> to <path> (<size>, <n> s).`, drops the seconds when
the file states none, and no cap, hold or charge reads that number.

# Configuration

Every option is optional. The plugin reads them from `opencode.json`:

```json
{ "plugins": [{ "package": "github:joe-broadhead/opencode-elevenlabs#v0.0.3", "options": { "access": "all" } }] }
```

## Options

| Option | Values | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `access` | `"all"`, `"ask-changes"`, `"read-only"` | `"all"` | The permission posture the generated default rules express. |
| `region` | `"global"`, `"us"`, `"eu"`, `"in"`, `"sg"` | `"global"` | Which ElevenLabs environment's MCP server to register. Changing it needs a new sign-in. |
| `sessionCreditCap` | a whole number of credits, or `null` | `null` (no cap) | Opt-in: the most one session may spend. |
| `dailyCreditCap` | a whole number of credits, or `null` | `null` (no cap) | Opt-in: the most this plugin may spend in a rolling 24 hours in this data directory, across sessions, scripts and restarts. Two machines do not share it. |
| `mediaRoot` | a path, `~` for your home folder | `"~/Downloads/elevenlabs"` | Where `elevenlabs_save_media` writes. Created on first use with mode 0700. |
| `maxMediaBytes` | a whole number of bytes | `209715200` (200 MB) | The largest file the save tool writes. |
| `conversations` | `"full"`, `"summary"`, `"off"` | `"full"` | How much of a call's history the conversation reads may return. |
| `allowUntestedHost` | `true`, `false` | `false` | Start on an OpenCode version outside `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0`, with a note in status. |

Caps are opt-in. With neither set, the plugin refuses, cuts and queues nothing for money: ElevenLabs refuses a call the
workspace's balance cannot pay for, and the permission rules decide whether a paid call runs at all. `0` is refused for
either cap, because a typo in a cap you set must not be read as some other bound; leave the option out, or write `null`,
for no cap.

In Jelly, every option above except `mediaRoot` and `allowUntestedHost` is a setting, drawn with these values and
bounds. Jelly saves no `null`, so a cap there is no cap by being left unset.

## Spending

Twelve tools can bill the workspace: `creative_generate_speech`, `creative_generate_image`, `creative_generate_video`,
`creative_edit_image`, `creative_generate_in_flow`, `creative_run_flow_nodes`, `creative_transcribe_audio`,
`creative_design_voice`, `agents_run_tests`, `agents_compute_kb_rag_index`, `agents_query_knowledge_base_rag` and
`creative_create_brand_kit_from_website`. A price is ElevenLabs' own figure: the same call with `estimate_only: true`.
There is no rate table in this plugin. Every paid result carries a cost line, with or without a cap.

The first seven take `estimate_only`. The other five do not, so with no cap they run unpriced, and while a cap you set
is on they are refused (`PRICE_UNKNOWN`). The last three are counted as
spending because ElevenLabs' catalogue says neither way about them and they describe server-side work it plausibly
bills — embedding a knowledge-base document, running a RAG query, reading a public website — and the plugin counts
silence against the owner's money rather than for it.

With no cap, no estimate is sent before a paid call: no flow or node is left in the workspace for it, and the call
raises no permission prompt beyond its own. It runs at whatever size it asks for, calls of one method run side by side,
and each is recorded at the figure its result reports, or its cost line says `Credits: not reported`. An explicit
`estimate_only` call still answers with ElevenLabs' figure, and is never reported as a charge.

While a cap you set is on, the plugin sends the estimate itself before each paid call.

While a cap you set is on, a priced call is clamped to the number of generations the caps afford, **reserved** in the
ledger before it is sent, and settled into a charge when its result arrives, so two calls that start together cannot
both spend the same budget. A failure is charged the reserved price. The daily cap is one total for this data
directory; two machines do not share it.

A call the plugin cannot price is refused with `PRICE_UNKNOWN` while a cap is on, never run unpriced: a failed or
missing estimate, an argument ElevenLabs' own schema for that tool does not have, a `creative_*` name the table does not
know, and the five spending tools ElevenLabs offers no estimate for — `creative_design_voice`, `agents_run_tests`,
`agents_compute_kb_rag_index`, `agents_query_knowledge_base_rag` and `creative_create_brand_kit_from_website`.

Under a cap, the estimate is sent only where the paid call could run, because it is a call of its own: it costs nothing, but it
creates a flow and a node in the workspace. Under `access: "ask-changes"` the permission you answer is the generation's
own, and nothing is estimated if you refuse. That permission is asked twice for one paid call — once before the
estimate, once for the generation — so you may see two prompts for it; whether OpenCode folds them into one is
OpenCode's to decide and this plugin has not measured it. The figure is then remembered for ten minutes, so the paid
call does not ask for a second one.

`access: "read-only"` denies every tool that can spend, `creative_transcribe_audio` included: a transcription runs on a
node in a flow, and billing a workspace is not a read.

## Files outside the project

`elevenlabs_save_media` writes under `mediaRoot`, which is outside the project, so **two rules** apply: the tool's own
permission (`elevenlabs_save_media`) and OpenCode's `external_directory` rule for the folder.

```json
{ "permissions": [
  { "action": "elevenlabs_save_media", "resource": "*", "effect": "allow" },
  { "action": "external_directory", "resource": "/absolute/path/of/your/mediaRoot/*", "effect": "allow" }
] }
```

The second rule's resource is the **absolute** path of `mediaRoot` followed by `/*`; the default root is
`~/Downloads/elevenlabs`, and `~` is expanded to your home folder (the status report prints the expanded path). A refusal
whose message begins `permission.rejected: external_directory`, or that starts `EXTERNAL_DIRECTORY_DENIED`, needs that
rule; the plugin's own refusal prints the exact path to paste.

## Errors

Every code the plugin raises, in the order the table lists them:

| Code | What happened | Next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BALANCE_UNAVAILABLE` | The optional API key could not read the subscription. | Run `/elevenlabs-status`; if it keeps failing, remove the key in `/connect`. |
| `EXTERNAL_DIRECTORY_DENIED` | The save tool's `external_directory` rule is not allowed for the media folder. | Add `{ "action": "external_directory", "resource": "<absolute mediaRoot>/*", "effect": "allow" }` to the agent's rules. |
| `HOST_UNTESTED` | OpenCode is outside `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0`. | Use a supported OpenCode, or set `"allowUntestedHost": true`. |
| `MEDIA_EXPIRED` | The generated file's signed link has expired. | Fetch the generation again for a fresh link; do not generate again. |
| `MEDIA_TOO_LARGE` | The file is larger than `maxMediaBytes`. | Raise `maxMediaBytes` if you mean to keep a file this large. |
| `MEDIA_URL_INVALID` | The link is not `https`, carries credentials, or is not on ElevenLabs' generated-file host. | Pass the link a generation returned. |
| `OPTIONS_INVALID` | A plugin option is missing, of the wrong type, or out of range. | Fix the option; the message names the accepted values. |
| `PRICE_UNKNOWN` | A call that may spend cannot be priced, and a cap you set is on, so it was refused before it was sent. | Price it first with `"estimate_only": true` where the tool takes it, or set both caps to `null` — the refusal's next step says which. |
| `RULES_NOT_ADDED` | The default rules could not be inserted into the agents. | Restart OpenCode. |
| `SAVE_FAILED` | The file could not be written, or the folder changed while it was. | Check `mediaRoot`, its permissions, and the `external_directory` rule. |
| `SERVER_NOT_REGISTERED` | The MCP server could not be registered. | Restart OpenCode. |
| `SKILLS_INVALID` | A skill file is missing or malformed. | Reinstall the plugin. |
| `SPEND_CAP_REACHED` | The call would exceed the `sessionCreditCap` or `dailyCreditCap` you set, or, under that cap, a priced call of the same method is already in flight. | Raise the cap, set it to `null`, wait for the 24-hour window to roll, or wait for the in-flight call to return or for its ten-minute reservation to run out. |
| `STATUS_UNAVAILABLE` | The status report could not be read. | Restart OpenCode, then run `/elevenlabs-status` again. |

An upstream error from ElevenLabs passes through unchanged, a `429` rate limit included: wait for the window it names.
